lesson_title: Measurement, Maps, Data and Probability Essentials: Buy Enough, Not Too Much
hook_text: The maths says 11,2 boxes of tiles. Buy 11 and you FAIL the floor. Here's the rounding rule shops never teach.
clip_script: The lounge floor: 4,8 by 3,5 — 16,8 square metres of tiling to do. Boxes cover 1,5 square metres each, so the job needs 11,2 boxes. And here is the whole topic in one decision: you cannot buy 0,2 of a box, and 11 boxes leaves bare floor by the door. Twelve boxes. Always UP, never nearest — the shop rounds your money up in its favour; you round the boxes up in the floor's favour. Twelve at R189: R2 268 on the list. Paint plays the same game with a twist: 16 square metres of wall, but TWO coats means the brush travels 32 — the quiet detail buried mid-sentence that doubles the answer. Measure, match units, round up to what the shop actually sells, price it.
visual_style: Tiles snapping onto a floor grid that stops one patch short at 11 boxes, the bare patch flashing red by the door, then a twelfth box sliding in to complete it as the total price stamps down.
pacing: Quick area build, tense freeze on the bare patch, clean resolve with the round-up rule and price stamp.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision lesson to cost, map, summarise and judge like an examiner.
